primitives.name: Topic Grouping and Ranking
primitives.verbatim_quote: The ranking system groups documents of a search result based on their relatedness, meaning that they are directed to similar topics.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'G': 'set of document groups', 'D_g': 'documents in group g', 'T': 'set of topics'}
primitives.assumptions: Documents are clustered by semantic similarity; each group represents a distinct topic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When topic overlap exceeds threshold, group boundaries become ambiguous.

layer2.mapping: Maps document sets to topic clusters via cosine similarity in TF-IDF space for diversity enforcement.
layer2.telemetry: Group coherence score (average intra-cluster cosine similarity)

primitives.name: Information Richness Selection
primitives.verbatim_quote: The ranking system selects the document from each group that has the highest information richness of the documents within the group.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I(d)': 'information richness of document d', 'd_max': 'document with max I(d) in group G'}
primitives.assumptions: Information richness correlates with content entropy or keyword density.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When all documents in a group have equal I(d), selection becomes arbitrary.

layer2.mapping: Selects top-k documents per group based on normalized information gain metric.
layer2.telemetry: Average information gain per selected document

primitives.name: Diversity Enforcement
primitives.verbatim_quote: The ranking system ranks the documents to ensure that the highest ranking documents may include at least one document covering each topic, that is, one document from each of the groups.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R': 'ranking function', 'r_i': 'rank position i', 'd_i': 'document at rank i'}
primitives.assumptions: Each topic must be represented once among top-ranked documents.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If number of groups exceeds top-K, diversity constraint cannot be satisfied.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to multi-armed bandit problem where arms are topic groups.
layer2.telemetry: Number of unique topics covered in top-N results

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that search result ranking should balance information richness with topical diversity. The system models documents as elements of topic groups, where each group corresponds to a semantic cluster. Within each group, the document with maximum information richness is selected. These selections are then ordered to ensure that each topic is represented at least once in the top-K results. This process enforces a dual objective: maximizing relevance (via information richness) and minimizing redundancy (via diversity). Mathematically, this resembles a constrained optimization problem where the objective function is the sum of information gains across selected documents, subject to a diversity constraint ensuring one document per topic group. The failure mode occurs when topic overlap is high or when the number of groups exceeds the desired rank length, leading to suboptimal coverage.
